reasons: Complete 1264-character working original contains three explanatory whereas paragraphs, one operative paragraph (753:1201), and signature/date. The inventory override includes both the dispositive termination and its express saving sentence; nothing operative is omitted. The recited investigation/declaration belongs to the prior stay, not a new duty created by EO6847A.

At characters 753:1201 the order says "do hereby order that the stay of the provisions of Section 1 of Article IX of such Code be terminated." No delayed date, future notice, implementation, officer action or unsatisfied condition qualifies this disposition. The complete text ends "September 14, 1934", matching APP node 373333 metadata date/listing_date 1934-09-14. Thus first_end and whole_order_end 1934-09-14 are supported as completion of this present dispositive act, not signature alone.

The full parent EO6734A, dated June 9, 1934 (text hash 5618966120e4da22f9b1f1423ca7875d66cc2357aaf1f904d7d0aa7eb18bee56), places Article IX under the Secretary's emergency determination. EO6847A expressly removes only Section 1's stay and saves the remainder of the June 9 approval. The saving sentence defines the exception's boundary; it creates no separate performance or continuing enforcement delegation in EO6847A. This is express termination, not a strike-and-insert amendment of continuing wording.

No report, appointment, payment, investigation or future repeat act is directed by this complete order. The target is the September termination act, not the June stay's entire prior lifecycle. An earlier determination affecting the parent could change parent-code operation but would not move completion of this newly expressed termination act before its issuance.

The code's released operation and the expressly saved parent provisions are consequences outside the exhausted act. The claim does not establish that parent provisions remained valid through 2026 or adjudicate accrued rights/liabilities. The transferred_or_accrued explanation preserves that limitation rather than claiming universal statutory savings.

Schechter (May 27, 1935) and S.J.Res.113 (June 14, 1935) postdate the completed September 1934 act. The latter separately repeals code approval/enforcement and extends remaining Title I; neither supplies this first ending. The additional held EO6999 of March 30, 1935 transfers specified wheat-flour administrative powers, retaining Agriculture limits; it neither reopens this disposition nor gives EO6847A a new pending command. Shared EO7076/7252 continuation propositions likewise supply no reason to postpone its completed act.

Subject to the expressly preserved provisional-source replacement obligation and bounded search limits, the exact claim supports whole_order_status no with no material unresolved performance question.

The assertion that the printed date and matched APP metadata establish Jun. 14, 1935 is factually false. Both establish December 19, 1934. This is a material first-ending error, not a source formatting defect.

reasons: Complete 1367-character working original independently read. Characters 749:1188 contain the adoption/approval of the already rendered cancellation report and "do hereby cancel my order approving said Code." The recital affirmatively states that the public hearing was held and the Board rendered its report; it does not commission future reporting. The full operative inventory is included by the override.

The held text, its quotation within the exact claim, and APP node 373464 metadata all date EO6925A December 19, 1934. MIRROR_DOCUMENTS date and listing_date are 1934-12-19. Its full operative paragraph has no June 1935 effective clause or other deferred trigger. Present adoption and cancellation therefore support completion on 1934-12-19, not the claimed 1935-06-14.

Full EO6543J (text hash bca1546fa78673b4544912a98f9c62d0e78e4ba9cf3b03d5d0e0df21edeeb988) approves the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade code on December 30, 1933; its APP heading/date confirm the target identified in EO6925A. The recited Trucking and Construction Codes describe consequences under their own approvals, rather than new approvals or future transfer commands issued by EO6925A.

The cancellation's continuing effect, other codes' potential operation and unresolved accrued-rights questions are distinct from performance of the adoption/cancellation. The residual discussion does not itself establish liability preservation and is appropriately limited. None supplies an event extending this order's dispositive act to June 14, 1935.

S.J.Res.113 is actually approved June 14, 1935 and repeals specified code powers, but is disclosed only as a later source note and does not supply a deferred effective term for EO6925A. Schechter also postdates the December cancellation. Generic shared research cannot override the target's explicit date. The exact claim fails whole-case review even though its text custody, inventory and basic completion mechanism are otherwise supported.
